stories.headline: HSBC's Sels Rotates Away from Semiconductors into Applications and Cloud
stories.what_happened: On semiconductors, HSBC Private Bank's Global CIO Willem Sels says, "in terms of delays and in thinking about how different parts of the stack react to the delays, therefore do we change our positioning? And I think we do. We have done so: we are much more in the cloud and in the applications." He speaks to Bloomberg's Tom Mackenzie, Anna Edwards, and Guy Johnson on "The Opening Trade." (Source: Bloomberg)

stories.headline: ECB's Kazāks Sees Rate-Hike Judgments Getting ‘More Nuanced’
stories.what_happened: Latvia Central Bank Governor Mārtiņš Kazāks said further monetary tightening may be necessary if elevated energy prices persist and risk spilling into broader inflation. In an interview with Bloomberg TV on Tuesday, he added that policy trade-offs are becoming increasingly nuanced as officials have to balance price stability against the danger of undermining economic growth. Focus instead on getting the house you want, then refinance when rates inevitably came down. Michelle Amponsah reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

stories.headline: Fed's Waller Supports Rate Hike in December
stories.what_happened: Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said he supports an interest-rate hike in December, and warned that if inflation continues to accelerate he would support a half-percentage-point increase to protect the central bank’s credibility. “If inflation comes in substantially higher than I expect, more robust action by the FOMC may be called for,” Waller said at the Bank of England and Its Watchers event. (Source: Bloomberg)

stories.headline: US Treasury yields rise as Fed's Waller presses rate hike case
stories.what_happened: Following remarks from Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller, short-dated Treasury yields saw an uptick, as he proposed the necessity of action despite seemingly moderated inflation data. Waller highlighted a possible half-point rate increase if inflation intensifies, signaling potential shifts in monetary policy. Economists expect a modest rise in core inflation, guiding market anticipations as money markets now fully reflect a 25 basis point increase in December.

stories.headline: Bajaj Finance issues 5.74 crore warrants to promoter for Rs 5,799 crore
stories.what_happened: Bajaj Finance has allotted 5.74 crore warrants to its promoter, Bajaj Finserv, for Rs 5,799 crore. The special committee of the board approved the issue at an issue price of Rs 1,010 per warrant. Each warrant is convertible into an equivalent number of equity shares of the company. A minimum of 25 percent of the consideration is payable at allotment, while the remaining 75 percent will be payable later.

stories.headline: FPIs turn net buyers; pour Rs 53,739 crore in D-Street in Nov so far
stories.what_happened: In November, foreign investors reversed a trend of selling by making substantial purchases of Indian equities. This shift followed a global sell-off triggered by AI developments affecting markets worldwide, including the US and Asia. The allure of strong domestic earnings growth alongside attractive valuations in large-cap stocks reignited investor interest in India, particularly in the financial services and technology sectors, with noteworthy activity also seen in the debt market.

stories.headline: Eurozone bond yields fall as lower energy prices ease inflation concerns
stories.what_happened: On Tuesday, government bond yields in the Eurozone experienced a notable drop, particularly for French and Italian bonds. The easing of inflation worries, attributed to falling oil and natural gas prices, enhanced demand for bonds. Germany's 10-year bond yield fell to 3.25%, while France's decreased to 4.69%. Boosted by the US President's calming remarks, market sentiment improved, especially for nations that had faced challenges in their bond markets.

stories.headline: California’s proposed ‘billionaire tax’ fails to pass
stories.what_happened: California voters rejected Proposition 40, the one-time 5% tax on billionaires, the AP reported Monday. Tech leaders outspent backers roughly 10 to 1 to defeat it, and the founders and economists TechCrunch interviewed before the vote were split on whether it would have driven out wealthy residents or just trimmed their fortunes.

stories.headline: Blood RNA signal may reveal ovarian cancer precursors before invasive disease develops
stories.what_happened: Hoag researchers have discovered a molecular warning signal in the blood that identifies serous tubal intraepithelial carcinoma (STIC), an early, precancerous stage of high-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC). This advance is particularly significant because ovarian cancer is often diagnosed at an advanced stage, after the disease has already spread.

stories.headline: Severe premenstrual mood disorder has three subtypes, symptom diaries suggest
stories.what_happened: Premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD) is a common mood disorder associated with the menstrual cycle. A new study published in Nature Communications shows that PMDD does not follow any universal pattern and that there are three subtypes with different patterns of symptoms. The hope is that this discovery will lead to more individualized treatment.

stories.headline: Immune proteins offer new clues to how prostate cancer could be prevented
stories.what_happened: A new study led by researchers at Oxford Population Health shows that higher levels of proteins involved in activating and coordinating the immune system were associated with a lower risk of developing prostate cancer. The findings suggest that the body's ability to recognize and respond to abnormal cells may play an important role in the early development of prostate cancer and could point to new approaches for preventing the disease.
